The search points primarily to one new paper and pages discussing it:

1. **EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents** — Primary arXiv paper, submitted October 12, 2026. It proposes a meta-agent that jointly adapts the training environment, user simulator, rewards, and agent configuration.  
   **People:** Min Cai — University of Alberta; Dan Zhang — National University of Singapore; Gao Xing and Libin Ma — Kuaishou Technology; Zhaohui Xu — independent researcher; Xi Ye — University of Alberta and Alberta Machine Intelligence Institute (Amii).  
   **URL:** [arxiv.org/abs/2610.16523](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16523)

2. **EAU project page** — Companion site linked from the paper; intended to provide project materials and presentation of the method.  
   **People/affiliations:** Same research team and affiliations listed above.  
   **URL:** [eau-meta-agent.github.io](https://eau-meta-agent.github.io/)

3. **Pith review of EAU** — An AI-generated critical review. It highlights the reported performance gains but questions unmatched compute budgets and dependence on proprietary meta-agents.  
   **People:** The same six paper authors; review produced through Pith using a DeepSeek model. Author affiliations are those listed above.  
   **URL:** [pith.science/paper/2610.16523](https://pith.science/paper/2610.16523)

4. **Min Cai’s research page** — Lead author’s page announcing EAU and describing it as a framework for co-evolving agents with their learning environments.  
   **People:** Min Cai — PhD student at the University of Alberta, supervised by Xi Ye; the page also notes prior research roles at Baidu and Z.ai.  
   **URL:** [henrycai11.github.io](https://henrycai11.github.io/)

1. **arXiv paper — “EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents.”**  
   Min Cai — University of Alberta; Dan Zhang — National University of Singapore; Gao Xing and Libin Ma — Kuaishou Technology; Zhaohui Xu — independent researcher; Xi Ye — University of Alberta and Alberta Machine Intelligence Institute (Amii).  
   https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16523

2. **Official EAU project page.**  
   Same six-person research team and affiliations listed above; linked directly from the paper.  
   https://eau-meta-agent.github.io/

3. **Pith paper review and technical breakdown.**  
   Covers the work by Cai, Zhang, Xing, Ma, Xu, and Ye, with the affiliations above. Pith highlights the framework’s reported gains but questions the lack of compute-matched comparisons; its displayed review was generated by a DeepSeek-V4-Flash AI referee.  
   https://pith.science/paper/2610.16523

1. **EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents** — The direct match. Introduces a meta-agent that jointly adapts the user simulator, environment, rewards, and RL configuration.  
   **People:** Min Cai — University of Alberta; Dan Zhang — National University of Singapore; Gao Xing and Libin Ma — Kuaishou Technology; Zhaohui Xu — independent researcher; Xi Ye — University of Alberta and Alberta Machine Intelligence Institute (Amii).  
   **URL:** [arXiv paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16523) · [Project site](https://eau-meta-agent.github.io/)

2. **EAU paper review and technical breakdown — Pith** — Independent AI-generated assessment of the EAU paper, highlighting its reported gains while questioning whether baseline compute budgets were matched.  
   **People:** Same six paper authors and affiliations listed above; review generated by a DeepSeek model rather than a named human reviewer.  
   **URL:** [Pith review](https://pith.science/paper/2610.16523)

3. **The Next Paradigm Is User-Centric Agent, Not Platform-Centric Service** — Closely related position paper proposing user-controlled, privacy-oriented agents operating through a device–cloud architecture. It is about the broader user-centric-agent paradigm, not the EAU meta-agent itself.  
   **People:** Luankang Zhang, Hang Lv, Qiushi Pan, Kefen Wang, Yonghao Huang, Xinrui Miao, Yin Xu, Hao Wang, and Enhong Chen — University of Science and Technology of China and the State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence; Wei Guo and Yong Liu — Huawei Technologies.  
   **URL:** [arXiv paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.15682)

1. **EAU project page — “Environment–Agent–User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents.”** Evaluates EAU on UserGym, ColBench, and τ²-bench, reporting substantial gains on ColBench. People: Min Cai (University of Alberta), Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore), Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology), Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher), and Xi Ye (University of Alberta and Amii).  
   URL: [https://eau-meta-agent.github.io/](https://eau-meta-agent.github.io/)

2. **EAU paper on arXiv — arXiv:2610.16523.** Primary research paper describing the meta-agent framework and its UserGym/ColBench experiments. Same authors and affiliations as above; Min Cai and Dan Zhang are marked as equal contributors.

3. **EAU full-text HTML.** Browser-readable version containing the methodology, benchmark details, result tables, affiliations, and appendices.

text:
1. **EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents** — The closest match. A meta-agent modifies the user simulator, environment, rewards, and RL configuration during ongoing multi-turn training.  
   **People:** Min Cai (University of Alberta); Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore); Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology); Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher); Xi Ye (University of Alberta and Alberta Machine Intelligence Institute).  
   **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16523

2. **From Trainee to Trainer: LLM-Designed Training Environment for RL with Multi-Agent Reasoning** — Closely related: the current policy analyzes failures and redesigns the next stage’s RL environment, though changes occur between stages rather than live within a training run.  
   **People:** Chao Chen and Zhiwei Li (LARK, HKUST Guangzhou); Chengzu Li and Yinhong Liu (University of Cambridge); Zhijiang Guo (LARK, HKUST Guangzhou/HKUST).  
   **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17682

query: adaptive user simulator reward design LLM agents
text:
1. **UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning** — Directly studies how turn-level reward shaping, trajectory scoring, and simulator choice affect multi-turn LLM-agent training.  
   **People:** Cheng Qian, Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Jielin Qiu, Zhiwei Liu, Haolin Chen, Shirley Kokane, Heng Ji, Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Huan Wang.  
   **Affiliations:** Salesforce AI Research; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.  
   **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.19736](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.19736)

2. **Training Proactive and Personalized LLM Agents** — Introduces UserVille and a multi-objective reward combining task success, interaction effort, and preference adherence.  
   **People:** Weiwei Sun, Xuhui Zhou, Weihua Du, Xingyao Wang, Sean Welleck, Graham Neubig, Maarten Sap, Yiming Yang.  
   **Affiliations:** Carnegie Mellon University; OpenHands.  
   **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02208](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02208)

3. **UserLM-R1: Modeling Human Reasoning in User Language Models with Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning** — Builds adaptive profiles and goal-driven simulated users, then improves their strategic behavior using composite RL rewards.  
   **People:** Feng Zhang, Shijia Li, Chunmao Zhang, Zhanyu Ma, Jun Xu, Jiuchong Gao, Jinghua Hao, Renqing He, Jingwen Xu, Han Liu.  
   **Affiliations:** Meituan; Peking University; Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Dalian University of Technology.  
   **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.09215](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.09215)

4. **Learning User Simulators with Turing Rewards** — Proposes Turing-RL: an LLM judge rewards simulated responses according to how indistinguishable they are from a real user’s responses, rather than simple response matching.  
   **People:** Yingshan Susan Wang, Cedegao E. Zhang, Linlu Qiu, Zexue He, Pengyuan Li, Alex Pentland, Roger P. Levy, Yoon Kim.  
   **Affiliations:** MIT; Stanford University; MIT–IBM Watson AI Lab.  
   **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19336](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19336)

5. **LLM-Powered User Simulator for Recommender System** — Uses an interpretable combination of LLM-derived preference logic and statistical modeling to supply simulated engagement for RL recommender agents.  
   **People:** Zijian Zhang, Shuchang Liu, Ziru Liu, Rui Zhong, Qingpeng Cai, Xiangyu Zhao, Chunxu Zhang, Qidong Liu, Peng Jiang.  
   **Affiliations:** Jilin University; Kuaishou Technology; City University of Hong Kong; Xi’an Jiaotong University.  
   **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.16984](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.16984)

Co-evolves a tool-use policy and its training interface using diagnosed rollout failures.

3. **CoEvolve: Training LLM Agents via Agent-Data Mutual Evolution** (ACL 2026) — Shidong Yang, Ziyu Ma, Tongwen Huang, Yiming Hu, Yong Wang, and Xiangxiang Chu (AMAP, Alibaba Group). Alternates agent optimization with feedback-guided task and training-distribution evolution.  
   URL: [ACL Anthology PDF](https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.1055.pdf)

4. **GenEnv: Difficulty-Aligned Co-Evolution Between LLM Agents and Environment Simulators** (ICLR 2026) — Jiacheng Guo, Ling Yang, Jiahao Qiu, Ke Shen, and Mengdi Wang (Princeton); Peter Chen (Columbia); Qixin Xiao and Xinzhe Juan (University of Michigan); Yinjie Wang (University of Chicago). Co-trains an agent and a simulator that generates tasks near the agent’s current capability frontier.  
   URL: [OpenReview](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=5vsYRklFJf)

5. **Agent0: Unleashing Self-Evolving Agents from Zero Data via Tool-Integrated Reasoning** (Nov. 2025) — Peng Xia, Kaide Zeng, Jiaqi Liu, Yiyang Zhou, and Huaxiu Yao (UNC–Chapel Hill); Can Qin and Caiming Xiong (Salesforce Research); Fang Wu (Stanford). Co-evolves a curriculum-generating agent and a tool-using executor without curated training data.
